findings.text: the step row reads product(...) but product is bound only in the krylov and gmres arms of linear_step, so --method dense raises UnboundLocalError before the row is built; measure.py:945 accepts dense and six job scripts pass it, so those runs now crash where the base returned a step row.

the same unbound product reference sits in solver.py's linear_step: the dense arm binds products (plural) and lines 729 and 734 then read product, which symtable reports as a local of that function, so --method dense raises UnboundLocalError where the pre-change code read the factor returned by jax.linearize.

measure_warm builds its factor program with active_operands, but that name is the cold tuple assigned at measure.py:788 in the sibling compare branch; the warm operand set it actually computed is warm_operands at measure.py:837, and the two agree only because the warm path leaves active_operands untouched.

operand_tangent takes a point argument and never uses it, while the identically named helper at solver.py:71 closes over point; two helpers share a name and a docstring with incompatible contracts, so a reader moving between the two drivers is told the wrong thing.

the record carries the captured-constants, generated-bytes and host-RSS comparisons but no figure, and the brief's write list names docs/figures/converged-forward-solve/constant-capture; the before/after lowering comparison is the one relationship the record exists to show.

the node summary still says the measurement of the captured-constants total and the certificate rows is pending on SLURM job 1295096, while the sibling fragment reports those figures; the landed text states a pending state the run itself has since superseded.
baseline_suite and after_suite carry a <file> placeholder and a prose expansion in their command field, so neither records the literal command that ran and neither arm can be re-run from the record.
changed_paths omits docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/solve-operand-capture.html, which the diff against the base adds, so the record's path list understates what the node landed.
